title: Child Abuse Identification and Reporting Policy
text:
Vortex Athletics

Child Abuse Identification and Reporting Policy

Policy number VA 001 | Policy owner Owner or Managing Director

Effective date ____________________ | Approved by ____________________

1 Purpose and coverage

Vortex Athletics requires personnel to recognize and report suspected child abuse or neglect promptly and to protect anyone who raises a concern in good faith. A child is anyone younger than 18. This policy applies to employees, coaches, instructors, contractors, interns and volunteers, including concerns about any child, whether or not enrolled at Vortex. It covers facilities, travel, competitions, camps, private lessons, online contact and concerns learned outside regular operations. The alleged person may be a staff member, caregiver, athlete, peer or other individual.

This policy operates with the Vortex Athletics Abuse Prevention and Staff Boundaries Policy and Abuse and Harassment Crisis Management Plan. External reports must proceed even if an internal contact is unavailable. Section 7 provides a separate route for vulnerable adult concerns.

2 Individual responsibility to report

Every adult staff member must act when information gives reason to believe that a child may have experienced abuse or neglect. Proof, a visible injury, certainty, parental permission and management approval are not required. Staff must not investigate credibility, confront the alleged person or ask others to verify the story. Each adult must make the required external reports personally, even if someone else says a report has been made. Report additional relevant information when it becomes known.

Junior staff must immediately tell an uninvolved adult staff member or trusted adult and may also report directly to authorities. An adult who receives the concern must take responsibility for required reports. No victim is required by this policy to report their own abuse.

3 Immediate action sequence

Protect immediate safety. Call 911 for immediate danger, urgent medical needs or an imminent threat. Arrange safe, observable supervision and summon appropriate medical assistance.

Report immediately to appropriate law enforcement and Maryland Child Protective Services at 1-800-917-7383. Request CPS and identify where the child is and where the incident occurred. Vortex requires both contacts. If the appropriate police agency is uncertain, ask CPS or emergency dispatch for routing assistance without delaying the report.

Where USA Gymnastics or U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Movement reporting duties apply, report suspected child abuse directly to the U.S. Center for SafeSport immediately. Contact 833-587-7233 or use the online reporting page. Report to authorities before SafeSport. The 24 hour outer limit in applicable reporting rules is never permission to wait.

Notify the uninvolved Vortex safeguarding coordinator immediately after external reporting, or concurrently if another person can notify them without delay. Complete the written follow up in section 5 and the confidential incident record. Neither an internal form nor an internal notification replaces an external report.

Reporting resources: Maryland CPS and SafeSport reporting.

4 Identifying concerns and responding to disclosures

Staff must remain alert to physical abuse, sexual abuse or exploitation, mental injury or emotional abuse, and neglect. The following examples are recognition guidance; authorities determine legal definitions and whether an investigation is warranted.

Physical abuse and unsafe coaching

Concerns include unexplained or patterned injuries, explanations inconsistent with an injury, fear of a particular adult, hitting, shaking, aggressive restraint or painful punishment. Staff must report suspected harm from forced stretching, dangerous conditioning, training through a serious injury, or withholding water, food, toileting or necessary medical care. Routine sports participation does not excuse abusive conduct.

Sexual abuse and exploitation

Concerns include sexual contact, exposure, sexual requests, sexualized messages, requests for intimate images, exploitation or trafficking. Possible indicators include a disclosure, unexplained pain, sudden fear of a person or place, regression or sexual knowledge or behavior inconsistent with the child's development. Abuse may occur without an outward injury or a clear verbal disclosure.

Emotional harm and neglect

Concerns include threats, persistent humiliation, coercion, isolation, serious changes in behavior, inadequate supervision or unmet essential care that places a child at risk. Poverty, disability, cultural differences, appearance or a child's communication style alone do not establish neglect. Describe specific conduct and observed risks rather than making assumptions about a family.

Grooming and boundary violations

Secrecy, favoritism, gifts tied to a special relationship, isolating a child, private electronic contact, sexual jokes and repeated attempts to bypass supervision require prompt attention. Report prevention policy violations to the coordinator immediately and to the applicable sport body when required. If the information also creates suspicion of abuse or neglect, use the full external reporting sequence immediately. Staff must not wait for a pattern to develop.

Receiving a disclosure

Move to a calm setting that preserves appropriate visibility and immediate safety. Listen without expressing shock or disbelief. Allow the child to use their own words and communication method.

Say, "Thank you for telling me. You did the right thing. This is not your fault. I need to share this with people who can help keep you safe." Do not promise secrecy or a particular outcome.

Ask only minimal, open questions needed to identify immediate danger and make the report. Do not suggest answers, repeatedly question the child, request a written statement or ask the child to demonstrate what happened.

Record the child's words accurately as soon as possible. Distinguish direct observations, statements and information from other people. Do not delay a report to finish notes.

Seek direction from authorities about parent notification and safe pickup. Do not automatically alert a parent, caregiver or alleged person who may be implicated. Tell police immediately if release to a suspected abuser is imminent.

Recognition guidance: Maryland signs of abuse or neglect. Disclosure guidance: SafeSport reporting dos and donts.

5 Maryland oral and written reporting

Maryland Family Law section 5-705 requires people in Maryland with reason to believe a child has experienced abuse or neglect to notify local social services or appropriate law enforcement, subject to narrow legal exceptions. Section 5-704 sets additional duties for specified professionals, including health practitioners, police officers, educators and human service workers acting professionally.

Vortex requires every adult staff reporter to follow the immediate oral reporting sequence in section 3 and submit a written report to the appropriate local Department of Social Services within 48 hours of the contact or information that created the suspicion, with a copy to the local State's Attorney. This written procedure is a Vortex standard for all adult staff; section 5-704 independently requires it for the professionals covered by that law. The clock does not restart when a delayed oral report is made.

Use Maryland DHR SSA Form 180 or the format directed by the receiving agency. During the initial call, confirm the correct jurisdiction and secure written submission method for DSS and the State's Attorney. Mark unknown facts as unknown; missing details do not justify delay. Keep submission confirmations. Submit the written follow up even if CPS does not accept the concern for investigation. The Vortex incident record supports, and does not replace, this external report.

For incidents outside Maryland, or when the child's location is uncertain, contact authorities immediately, provide all known locations and follow directions about additional reports. Historical child abuse remains reportable to police and SafeSport under applicable Movement duties even if the victim is now an adult or the reporter learned the allegation before joining the Movement. The victim's exception from self reporting remains in place.

Authorities: Family Law 5 704, Family Law 5 705, and Maryland Form 180.

6 USA Gymnastics and SafeSport reports

For matters subject to Movement reporting duties, all suspected child abuse, including nonsexual abuse, must be reported directly to law enforcement and SafeSport immediately. Sexual misconduct must be reported directly to SafeSport immediately and no later than 24 hours; if a child is involved, the child abuse reporting route also applies. Reporting to Vortex or USA Gymnastics alone is insufficient.

Physical or emotional misconduct and prevention policy violations that do not create suspicion of child abuse must be reported promptly to USA Gymnastics or SafeSport as applicable, and to the Vortex coordinator. USAG reporting is available at 833-844-7233 or its reporting portal. Applicable Adult Participants must also report directly to SafeSport criminal charges or dispositions involving sexual misconduct or misconduct involving minors, suspected aiding and abetting or abuse of the Center's process, and retaliation. Let the Center resolve jurisdiction questions; do not reduce suspected child abuse to an internal behavior complaint.

Sport authorities: 2026 SafeSport Code section X and USA Gymnastics reporting portal.

7 Separate reporting route for vulnerable adults

A vulnerable adult under Maryland law is an adult who lacks the physical or mental capacity to meet daily needs. A diagnosis, age or disability alone does not establish incapacity. Vortex requires all staff to report suspected abuse, neglect, self neglect or exploitation immediately to Adult Protective Services at 1-800-917-7383, requesting APS. Call 911 for immediate danger and report suspected crimes to police. Involve the adult in safe decisions and respect lawful consent and autonomy.

This is a Vortex requirement for all staff. Maryland section 14 302 independently mandates reports by specified professionals. The child specific 48 hour written report and State's Attorney copy procedure does not apply to APS reports. Document the APS report internally and provide follow up requested by authorities. Maryland APS and Family Law 14 302.

8 Internal notification and protective action

The Owner or Managing Director must appoint and train a safeguarding coordinator and an alternate before implementation. Record their names and direct contact information below and make them accessible to staff. If either is implicated, unavailable or has a conflict, contact the other uninvolved leader directly. If no uninvolved leader is available, continue external reports and contact applicable sport authorities. No complaint may be routed only to the person accused.

The coordinator activates the Crisis Management Plan, arranges safe supervision, addresses access to children, and coordinates medical care and communications with authorities. Vortex may impose precautionary safety or employment restrictions consistent with the Center's jurisdiction and directions. These steps do not determine guilt. Staff must not confront the person, mediate the allegation, interview witnesses to establish credibility or conduct their own abuse investigation.

Coordinator name and direct phone __________________________________________

Alternate name and direct phone ____________________________________________

9 Documentation and confidential records

After immediate reports, the reporting staff member must complete the incident record before the end of the shift, or as soon as safely practicable. Record how the concern became known; dates, times and locations; the child's exact words; objective observations; known contact details for involved people and witnesses; immediate risks; protective steps; and each report recipient, time and reference number. Do not speculate or label an allegation substantiated.

The coordinator serves as records custodian unless an uninvolved replacement is appointed. Store original records in a restricted safeguarding file, separate from routine class records. Preserve relevant video before automatic deletion, messages and access logs without editing originals. Staff must not search personal devices, conduct bodily examinations, photograph intimate injuries, or download, copy or forward suspected child sexual abuse material. Tell police where such material is located and follow their instructions.

Limit information to authorities, authorized sport officials and personnel who need it to protect safety or fulfill duties. Do not promise absolute confidentiality. The custodian logs access and authorized production, follows legal holds and the approved retention schedule, and permits no deletion while an allegation, investigation, claim or legal hold remains open.

10 Protection training and accountability

Vortex prohibits retaliation, intimidation, interference, suppression of a report and requiring someone to withdraw a concern. Good faith reports remain protected when an allegation is unsubstantiated. Concerns about retaliation must be reported through the same independent routes.

All personnel must receive this policy and training before unsupervised duties, with refresher training at least annually and any additional required SafeSport education. The coordinator maintains training and acknowledgment records, checks reporting contacts annually and when they change, and reviews the policy after an incident or material legal change. Violations may result in restrictions, discipline or termination, consistent with law and required sport processes. No disciplinary process may delay an external report.

Staff acknowledgment

I have read this policy, know where reporting contacts are kept, and understand my duty to report promptly without waiting for internal permission. I understand the confidentiality and nonretaliation requirements.

Staff name __________________________ Signature __________________________

Date ____________________ Trainer or supervisor ___________________________

Source review date November 6 2026. Approval and effective date are recorded on page 1.

Confidential incident reporting record

Complete after immediate safety measures and external reports. This record is not a substitute for Maryland Form 180, a police report, a SafeSport report or an APS report. Use additional securely stored pages when necessary. Record unknown information as unknown.

title: Abuse Prevention and Staff Boundaries Policy
text:
Vortex Athletics

Abuse Prevention and Staff Boundaries Policy

Policy number VA 002  Policy owner Owner or Managing Director

Effective date ____________________  Approved by ____________________

Purpose and application

Vortex Athletics requires a safe environment for every participant. This policy establishes staff conduct, supervision, communication, and access requirements intended to prevent sexual abuse, grooming, and other misconduct. It applies to owners, managers, coaches, employees, contractors, volunteers, interns, and other authorized personnel, collectively called staff. It covers facilities, programs, competitions, camps, travel, digital communications, and relationships arising from a Vortex role outside operating hours.

Youth means a person under 18. Protections also extend to vulnerable adults, including adults whose physical or mental limitations prevent them from providing for their daily needs. Staff must respect each adult's dignity, privacy, lawful decision-making, and communication preferences. Disability alone does not establish incapacity. An adult's parent or caregiver does not automatically have authority to consent on that adult's behalf.

Zero tolerance for sexual abuse

Vortex prohibits sexual abuse, sexual exploitation, grooming, sexual harassment, retaliation, and knowingly enabling abuse. Staff must never initiate sexual or romantic contact with a youth participant or with a participant over whom they exercise coaching, supervisory, care, or other authority. Apparent agreement, parental permission, a participant's initiation, or a claimed misunderstanding of age does not excuse prohibited conduct. These standards apply on and off duty and through every communication medium.

Zero tolerance requires prompt reporting, immediate protective action, and appropriate consequences under fair procedures. It does not authorize staff to decide an allegation is true or false before reporting.

Appropriate physical contact

Contact must serve a legitimate instructional, safety, care, or brief celebratory purpose; remain visible, professional, and proportionate; and respect the participant's expressed boundaries. High fives, fist bumps, and brief side hugs may be appropriate when welcomed. Never require affection or use physical contact as a reward for compliance.

Before spotting, positioning, or assisting a stretch, explain the purpose and intended contact in age-appropriate language, seek the participant's agreement, and use the least contact needed. Use a different safe instructional method when possible if contact is declined. Immediate contact necessary to prevent a fall or serious injury is permitted; explain it afterward and document any concern or unusual contact.

Staff must not permit lap sitting, cuddle, tickle, wrestle, pinch, kiss, pull hair, give prolonged hugs, or touch to punish or humiliate. Sexualized contact is prohibited. Contact with breasts, groin or genitals is prohibited except necessary emergency assistance or expressly authorized personal care. Contact near sensitive areas during a recognized gymnastics safety spotting technique must be limited to what is necessary, explained and observable. Document unusual or concerning contact promptly and report any suspected abuse. Never use spotting as a pretext for unnecessary contact, continue nonessential contact after refusal or ask a participant to touch a staff member's body.

Language and emotional boundaries

Staff must use respectful, developmentally appropriate instruction. Sexual jokes, innuendo, comments about sexual development or attractiveness, body shaming, degrading nicknames, threats, and humiliation are prohibited. Staff must not show sexual material, request sexual images, discuss their own romantic or sexual experiences with participants, or invite participants to discuss sexual topics for personal gratification.

A participant's disclosure of abuse or a genuine health or safety question must be met calmly and professionally. Listen without interrogation, share only information needed for safety, and follow the reporting policy. Never promise secrecy. Staff must not make participants responsible for adult loneliness, relationship problems, finances, emotional needs, or personal crises.

Favoritism, secret agreements, exclusive friendships, private reward systems, and efforts to separate a participant from protective adults are prohibited. Team recognition and ordinary encouragement must follow consistent program practices. Personal gifts, cash, loans, and special favors are prohibited; modest items distributed through an approved team or program reward system are permitted.

Electronic communication and social media

Use Vortex-approved channels for legitimate program business. Communications with youth must include their parent or legal guardian, an adult immediate family member, or another authorized adult participant. Group messages must meet the same requirement. If a youth sends a private message, add an appropriate adult before responding, except when immediate protective action is necessary. Preserve an abuse disclosure and report it; do not circulate it to a suspected offender or unsafe caregiver.

Staff must not exchange private direct messages, create secret accounts, use disappearing messages, conceal communication, or move conversations to gaming, fitness, or social platforms to avoid oversight. Personal accounts must not friend, follow, or privately connect with youth participants. Use approved official program pages and obtain required permission before publishing participant images.

Personal phones may access an approved business channel only when Vortex authorizes the use and records remain retrievable. Do not create personal photo libraries, personal cloud files or informal staff chats containing participant images or sensitive disclosures. If a disclosure arrives unexpectedly on a personal device, preserve it without redistribution and arrange secure handling with the records custodian; do not delete evidence. Do not photograph or record anyone changing, undressed, receiving intimate care, or in a restroom or locker room. Preserve suspected unlawful material in place and obtain law enforcement instructions; do not copy, forward, or independently search for it.

For vulnerable adults, use accessible approved channels and transparent communication appropriate to the adult's consent and lawful support arrangements. Do not automatically include a parent or caregiver in private adult communications. Exploitative, sexualized, coercive, or secret staff contact is prohibited regardless of age.

Contact outside scheduled programs

Staff must not privately arrange babysitting, tutoring, sleepovers, social outings, home visits, or other personal services with youth participants. Disclose a genuine preexisting family or community relationship to management before related contact occurs. Management must document applicable safeguards and any permitted arrangement; friendship developed through coaching is not a preexisting relationship. No arrangement waives reporting duties or permits abuse. Apply equivalent safeguards against coercion and exploitation when assisting vulnerable adults outside programs.

Supervision in higher risk spaces

Staff must keep individual instruction and meetings observable and interruptible, meaning another adult can see the interaction and readily stop it. Cameras and electronic viewing do not replace this requirement. Do not meet alone behind closed doors, in storage rooms, equipment areas, pits, secluded offices, vehicles, or hidden locations. Maintain supervision during arrival, dismissal, breaks, and transitions.

Individual youth training requires advance written parent or guardian consent renewed at least annually, permission for the parent or guardian to attend, and the visibility safeguards above. Consent may be withdrawn. Supervisors must monitor private lessons and prevent staff from creating isolated sessions before opening or after closing. Apply a comparable visible arrangement to work with vulnerable adults while preserving appropriate privacy and lawful consent.

Restrooms locker rooms and changing areas

Provide private or semi-private changing options respecting gender, disability, cultural, and privacy needs. Prohibit photographic and recording functions in these areas, including by participants. No surveillance cameras may record inside restrooms, showers, or changing spaces.

Assign designated staff to monitor entrances and conduct appropriate regular and unpredictable checks. Announce entry and avoid unnecessary viewing of bodies. Use two authorized adults when entering to monitor or assist whenever possible. Staff must not change clothes, expose themselves, or shower with youth participants. Staff must not be alone with a youth in these spaces for routine conversation, discipline, or care.

Arrange disability-related personal assistance in advance through a documented plan identifying the authorized helper, consent, necessary assistance, privacy protections, and oversight. Obtain the adult participant's own consent when they can provide it; verify any substitute decision-maker's authority. Do not assume staff may provide intimate care simply because assistance is requested. Address emergencies promptly and document any necessary departure from ordinary safeguards.

Health care and athletic treatment

Only qualified, authorized personnel may provide care within their competence. Vortex services must not include intimate examinations. Refer needs outside staff qualifications to medical services. Do not ask participants to undress for an injury check or examine intimate areas.

For manual therapy, taping, assisted stretching, massage, and other therapeutic or recovery modalities involving youth, keep treatment observable and interruptible with another authorized adult physically present and able to see the treatment throughout. Obtain written parent or guardian consent at least annually; allow consent to be withdrawn. Keep breasts, buttocks, groin, and genitals covered. Explain each step before contact and seek the participant's continuing assent. Permit parent observation, subject to applicable venue credential restrictions. Coaches and club owners must not massage youth participants, even if licensed massage therapists.

Licensed health-provider meetings must remain observable and interruptible, with another adult at the facility notified, management informed, and legally appropriate consent. No closed-door appointments are permitted except emergencies. Protect clinical confidentiality through suitable room arrangements. Do not delay emergency first aid to arrange ordinary consent or staffing.

Transportation overnight programs and camps

Vortex must approve program transportation and lodging in advance, identify responsible screened adults, and provide families with itineraries and contact arrangements. Obtain written parent or guardian consent for youth transportation and lodging at least annually and for material trip-specific arrangements. Maintain clear pickup authorization, attendance, headcounts, and transfer of supervision.

As a Vortex standard, staff must not transport a youth participant alone or share a sleeping room or bed with youth participants. A staff member acting as the parent or lawful guardian of their own child may perform ordinary parental duties. Any genuine preexisting relationship requiring an accommodation must be reviewed in advance under applicable law and governing sport rules. Parental permission alone does not waive Vortex restrictions. Emergency departures must be limited to what safety requires, promptly disclosed, and documented.

Use at least two authorized adults for room checks. Maintain visible supervision in camps, overnight activities, treatment areas, and transition periods. Participants must be able to contact a safe parent, guardian, or support person and obtain help without staff obstruction. Do not confiscate communication access to conceal concerns.

For vulnerable adults, plan accessible transport, sleeping arrangements, and assistance with the participant and any legally authorized decision-maker. Respect privacy and adult autonomy. Never use dependence on transportation or care to obtain favors, affection, secrecy, or access to money.

Screening training and authorized access

Before assigning access to participants, management must verify identity, relevant employment and references, required criminal screening, applicable registry clearances, and governing sport eligibility. Complete all state, role-specific, licensing, and membership requirements, including USA Gymnastics and SafeSport requirements when applicable. Do not assume an NCSI criminal screen includes a separate state child-abuse registry clearance. A clear screen does not replace supervision or reporting.

Staff must not perform duties requiring screening or training until requirements are complete. Maintain renewal and eligibility records, check disciplinary restrictions, and enforce exclusions or conditions imposed by authorities or sport bodies. Supervisors must control keys, access codes, visitors, and contractor access; prohibit unauthorized isolated contact.

Train staff before participant contact and at least annually on this policy, identifying abuse, reporting routes, disclosures, emergency response, and retaliation. Provide accessible reporting information to participants and families. Supervisors must conduct practical checks of communication practices, staffing, changing arrangements, and treatment safeguards. Correct gaps promptly and document corrective action without investigating an abuse allegation.

Reporting concerns and responding to violations

Report suspected abuse when information gives reason for concern; proof, management approval, or a criminal charge is not required. Act whether the concern involves staff, a participant, a caregiver, or someone outside Vortex. An internal report or belief that another person reported does not discharge personal external obligations. No victim must self-report their own abuse.

For immediate danger or urgent medical needs, call 911. For suspected child abuse or neglect, immediately report to law enforcement and Maryland child protective services through the local department of social services or 1-800-917-7383. Complete Vortex's written follow-up within 48 hours of the initial contact or information and meet recipient and submission requirements in the Child Abuse Identification and Reporting Policy. When USA Gymnastics or SafeSport jurisdiction applies, also report immediately to the U.S. Center for SafeSport at 833-587-7233 or its reporting website. Do not wait 24 or 48 hours to report.

Report suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or exploitation of a vulnerable adult immediately to Maryland Adult Protective Services through the same statewide number or local department. Vortex requires every adult staff member to make this report as a company rule, regardless of whether the employee's profession is a statutory mandatory reporter. Junior staff must alert an uninvolved adult and may report directly. The child-specific 48 hour written report and State's Attorney copy requirements do not apply to APS reports.

Immediately notify the Vortex safeguarding coordinator after external reporting, or concurrently without delay. Bypass anyone implicated or unavailable and contact the alternate or an uninvolved manager. Report other boundary violations immediately to the coordinator and applicable sport body. No manager may prohibit, screen, delay, or discourage reporting.

Protective action and investigation

Separate the participant from immediate risk, arrange safe supervision, preserve existing records, and follow the Abuse and Harassment Crisis Management Plan. Do not confront the accused, interview children or witnesses to establish facts, mediate abuse allegations, or conduct a credibility review. Coordinate permitted employment reviews with investigating authorities and sport bodies; do not investigate matters within SafeSport's exclusive jurisdiction. Interim restrictions are protective and do not determine guilt.

Share information only with authorities and people who need it to protect participants or perform authorized duties. Do not promise absolute confidentiality. Retaliation, intimidation, secrecy demands, evidence destruction, and interference are prohibited. Policy violations may result in restrictions, removal from duties, termination, or other action consistent with law and applicable procedures. An unsubstantiated good-faith report is not misconduct.

Administration and acknowledgment

Before implementation, the Owner or Managing Director must appoint and train a safeguarding coordinator and alternate. Distribute this policy, obtain acknowledgments, and review it annually and after significant changes with the reporting policy and crisis plan. Vortex adopts these additional restrictions as company standards; general consent forms and informal exceptions cannot weaken them.

Staff name ____________________  Signature ____________________  Date ____________________

Reference authorities

Reviewed November 6 2026. Maryland reporting law, Maryland Adult Protective Services, USA Gymnastics Safety and Response Policy, 2026 SafeSport Code, SafeSport reporting, and Minor Athlete Abuse Prevention Policies.

title: Abuse and Harassment Crisis Management Plan
text:
Vortex Athletics

Abuse and Harassment Crisis Management Plan

Effective date ____________________  Approved by ____________________

Policy number VA 003  Policy owner Owner or Managing Director

Review date ____________________

Purpose and activation

Vortex Athletics shall respond promptly to suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation, harassment, retaliation, and related threats affecting athletes, staff, volunteers, or visitors. This plan governs immediate protection, reporting, records, communications, cooperation, and support during an allegation or investigation. It applies at the facility, during travel and events, through electronic communications and to concerns learned outside regular operations. It supplements the Child Abuse Identification and Reporting Policy and the Abuse Prevention and Staff Boundaries Policy.

Any employee receiving a complaint or learning facts that reasonably suggest abuse shall activate this plan immediately. A complaint need not be written, signed, firsthand, or proven. The response shall address the safety of the affected person and others while preserving fair treatment and the authority of investigating agencies. A victim is not required to make a complaint about their own abuse.

Required appointments and readiness

Before implementation, Vortex Athletics shall appoint a trained Safeguarding Coordinator and an alternate, complete the appointment record on the final page, and distribute verified reporting contacts. Training shall cover reporting obligations, trauma informed responses, child and vulnerable adult protection, records preservation, privacy, conflicts, and cooperation with authorities. Appointment or training shall not be represented as complete until documented.

The Safeguarding Coordinator receives complaints, activates this plan, coordinates protective measures, and maintains the response timeline. The coordinator cannot screen, approve, or prevent an external report.

The alternate takes over when the coordinator is unavailable, implicated, or otherwise conflicted. If both are conflicted, staff report externally and notify an uninvolved owner or governing representative. No reporting deadline pauses.

The Records Custodian secures the case file, preserves evidence, maintains access and disclosure logs, and produces authorized records.

The Victim Liaison offers practical assistance and referrals, coordinates safe updates, and communicates the affected person's preferences without investigating the allegation.

The Spokesperson manages organizational statements and media inquiries. Every employee retains the right and duty to communicate with authorities and exercise other protected rights.

An uninvolved authorized leader makes employment and operational decisions, with appropriate advice. Any shared roles must be documented and free of conflicts.

Staff shall report concerns directly to the coordinator or alternate after or alongside required external reports. If either cannot be reached, staff shall continue reporting and protective action without waiting.

Immediate protection and external reporting

The first employee aware of imminent danger shall call 911, request necessary medical assistance, and obtain safe supervision. Staff shall interrupt unsafe activity without confronting an alleged abuser about the allegations. Keep the affected person away from the alleged person where safely and lawfully possible. Do not detain an adult, conduct an examination, or use force except as lawfully necessary for an emergency. If a child's proposed release presents immediate danger, contact law enforcement and follow its instructions.

For suspected child abuse or neglect, Vortex Athletics requires every adult staff member to make immediate, direct reports to both appropriate law enforcement and the local Department of Social Services child protection unit. Maryland's reporting framework permits notification to either agency; reporting to both is the Vortex Athletics rule. Call 1-800-917-7383 for Maryland child protection reporting assistance or use the verified local DSS contact. An internal report, attorney consultation, insurance notice, or belief that someone else reported does not replace a staff member's reporting responsibility.

Every adult staff reporter shall also send a written child abuse report to local DSS, with a copy to the local State's Attorney, within 48 hours of learning the facts creating the concern. This is a Vortex Athletics requirement for all adult staff. Maryland law separately imposes oral and written duties on specified professionals; their statutory 48 hour period begins with the contact, examination, attention, or treatment creating the belief. Comply with an earlier applicable deadline. Send known information without waiting to complete every field.

Where USA Gymnastics or Olympic and Paralympic Movement duties apply, report child abuse and sexual misconduct directly to SafeSport immediately; 24 hours is an outside limit, never permission to wait. Child abuse goes to police first, including historical abuse when the victim is now an adult. Report applicable criminal charges or dispositions involving sexual misconduct or misconduct involving minors, aiding and abetting or abuse of the Center's process, and retaliation directly to SafeSport. Report other misconduct and prevention violations to USAG or SafeSport as required. Nonsexual child abuse still follows every child abuse reporting step. Supply new relevant information promptly.

For suspected abuse, neglect, self neglect, or exploitation of a vulnerable adult, all adult staff shall report immediately to Maryland APS through local DSS or 1-800-917-7383 and request APS. This company rule extends beyond the professions specified in Maryland APS law. Call law enforcement for immediate danger or suspected crime. The child reporting 48 hour and State's Attorney requirements do not apply to APS reports. Disability alone does not establish vulnerability; report observed needs and let APS determine eligibility while respecting adult autonomy.

Protective measures during an investigation

The coordinator and uninvolved authorized leader shall promptly establish a written safety plan addressing the affected person, other participants, witnesses, and the alleged person. Measures may include reassignment, administrative leave, separation of schedules, and restrictions on access to minors, messaging systems, facilities, transportation or relevant records. Coordinate with investigating agencies and sport authorities. When SafeSport exercises jurisdiction, Vortex may use permitted safety and employment measures but must not issue a new sport suspension in response to those allegations. Notify USAG of organizational measures the same day so it can meet the Code's 72 hour notification requirement. Do not determine guilt through a temporary safety decision.

Identify who implements each measure, when it begins, and who checks compliance. Give the alleged person only the information needed to implement lawful restrictions and prevent interference. Do not arrange a meeting between the parties, request a retraction, or require mediation. Staff shall report attempted contact, intimidation, retaliation, evidence destruction, or breaches immediately. Reassess protection when circumstances change; do not wait for criminal charges to address current risk.

Case records and preservation

The receiving employee shall promptly create an objective record after immediate reports and emergency care. Distinguish direct observations, statements received, and unknown information. Record:

Who was involved, available contact details, ages, and present locations, including relevant parent or caregiver details.

What was observed or reported, the exact words used when possible, and relevant circumstances or injuries described without conducting an examination.

When and where events reportedly occurred, when the concern was learned, and how it came to the employee's attention.

Known witnesses and their available contact information, possible ongoing contact, and immediate safety concerns.

Each external report, recipient, date, time, report number, instructions, written submission, and follow up.

Protective decisions, responsible personnel, communications, assistance offered, and review dates.

The Records Custodian shall secure originals of relevant messages, attendance records, schedules, training records, and existing surveillance footage before routine deletion. Suspend ordinary destruction for potentially relevant material and record who collected or transferred it. Do not edit originals, circulate evidence through group messages, search personal devices, or interview witnesses to build a case. Do not copy, download, or forward suspected child sexual abuse imagery; preserve the device or account without further viewing and request law enforcement instructions.

Store case material in a restricted location separate from routine program records. Limit access to authorized personnel with a legitimate role and maintain an access and disclosure log. Preserve records under the approved retention schedule and any legal hold; no destruction while a hold or investigation remains active. The custodian shall produce records lawfully requested by authorities, with counsel's assistance where appropriate, without using legal review to delay mandatory reports or urgent protection.

Communications with affected people and families

The Victim Liaison shall acknowledge the concern promptly, explain immediate next steps, identify a safe contact method, and ask about communication, accessibility, interpreter, and support needs. Use calm, respectful language. Listen without blame, repeated questioning, promises of secrecy, or assurances about the outcome. Explain that necessary information will be shared with responsible authorities and designated personnel.

Offer the affected person choices wherever possible, including a support person, different coach or schedule, breaks from activities, and assistance locating qualified medical, counseling, advocacy, or child advocacy services. Offer referrals without claiming Vortex Athletics has retained providers or guaranteeing payment. Avoid requiring repeated retelling, direct contact with the alleged person, or participation in an internal interview to receive support. Respect a competent adult's choices and obtain consent for optional referrals; involve a lawful representative only when safe and appropriate.

Coordinate parent or guardian notification with law enforcement or protective services. Do not automatically contact a parent or caregiver who may be implicated or whose notification may increase danger. Document agency guidance, who will notify the family, the timing, and any safety restrictions. Give families practical information about protection, reporting contacts, support options, and a designated update contact without disclosing other people's private information. Do not promise an investigation timetable or access to confidential findings.

Staff and public communications

The coordinator shall give staff the minimum information needed to implement safety measures and explain where concerns should be reported. Tell relevant personnel who is covering duties and whom to contact without sharing allegations unnecessarily. Prohibit gossip, intimidation, and unauthorized sharing of case records. These limits shall not restrict lawful reporting, cooperation with investigators, protected workplace discussions, or access to personal legal advice.

The Spokesperson shall coordinate factual organizational statements with counsel and investigating authorities when appropriate. A statement may acknowledge a reported concern, confirm that safety and reporting procedures have been activated, and provide a reporting contact. Do not identify an affected minor, speculate, declare guilt or innocence, discuss witness accounts, or release details that may compromise safety or the investigation. Refer media requests to the spokesperson and record significant inquiries and responses.

The liaison and coordinator shall agree with affected people on a reasonable update method and frequency and record it. Provide updates when material safety arrangements change, even if investigative details cannot be shared. Never demand silence, a nondisclosure agreement, release of claims, or withdrawal of a report as a condition of protection or support. Good faith reporting and cooperation shall not result in retaliation, reduced opportunities, threats, or adverse treatment.

Cooperation and professional advice

Vortex Athletics shall cooperate with law enforcement, CPS, APS, SafeSport, USA Gymnastics, and other authorities having jurisdiction. The coordinator shall record agency contacts, assign responsibility for each lawful request, preserve requested material, and arrange safe access to facilities or records. Staff shall provide truthful information and report new relevant facts directly when required. Do not coach witnesses, coordinate accounts, or obstruct private communications with investigators.

Law enforcement, protective services, and governing sport authorities control their respective investigations. Staff shall not undertake an internal abuse fact investigation or assess credibility. Counsel shall coordinate any permitted or legally required workplace review with relevant authorities. For harassment or policy matters outside reserved jurisdiction, appoint a qualified, uninvolved reviewer, define the scope, protect witnesses and provide a fair opportunity to respond. The reviewer must not interview a child about abuse or interfere with an external investigation. Necessary safety action and reporting continue throughout.

After immediate protection and external reports, an uninvolved authorized leader shall contact qualified counsel and the applicable insurer or broker the same day. Follow any earlier policy notice requirement and document notification, requested information, response deadlines, and instructions. Preserve evidence and obtain required approvals for coverage related arrangements without delaying care, protection, or reporting. Do not promise coverage, reimbursement, absolute confidentiality, or attorney privilege. Do not make an unauthorized admission of liability, settlement, or payment commitment; this does not restrict truthful reporting, compassionate acknowledgment, or lawful assistance.

Monitoring and closure

The coordinator shall monitor reporting completion, protective restrictions, support needs, response deadlines, and retaliation risks while the matter remains active. An agency declining a report or closing a case does not automatically eliminate other reporting duties or safety concerns. Document referrals and follow instructions without abandoning an immediate danger response.

An uninvolved authorized leader shall approve changes to protective measures after considering authority directives and current risk, with counsel as appropriate. Document the reason, responsible person, communication plan, and review date. Do not automatically restore unrestricted access when a case closes. Preserve applicable records and continue needed support. Review the response after closure and at least annually to correct contact details, training gaps, and procedural failures without unnecessarily identifying affected people.

Appointment and training record

The Safeguarding Coordinator also serves as crisis coordinator. The Owner or Managing Director must complete appointments and verify training before implementation. The same individual may hold multiple roles only when able to perform them without conflict.
